title: G6PD Activity Assay Protocol
author: Wen Aw
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rwbd7an
materials: Protein concentration is determined by Bradford Assay

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make lysis buffer containing 20 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0), 3 mM magnesium chloride, 1 mM EDTA, 0.02 % β‑mercaptoethanol, protease inhibitor, and 0.1 % Triton X‑100.

steps.title: Homogenize larvae
steps.instruction: Homogenize 2 larvae in 40 µL of the prepared lysis buffer.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 16,000 g for 15 min at 4 °C and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Make NADPH standards
steps.instruction: Prepare NADPH standard solutions ranging from 0 mM to 0.3 mM in the same buffer used for the assay.

steps.title: Prepare reaction mix with NADP+
steps.instruction: For each assay well, add NADP+ to achieve the required concentration.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.5 µL of 80 mM NADP+ solution.
Add 37.5 µL of Tris buffer (to bring the volume to 40 µL).

steps.title: Add sample to wells
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the cleared larval supernatant (or NADPH standard) to each well, bringing the total volume to 50 µL.

steps.title: Start enzymatic reaction
steps.instruction: Initiate the reaction by adding 50 µL of substrate solution containing either G6P + 6PGL (both at 5 mM final concentration) or 6PGL alone (5 mM final concentration).
